hits.name: Ethan Mollick
hits.hook: Mollick on the agentic bank-run thesis: systems that only work because of friction are about to get stress-tested.
hits.draft_en:
Ethan Mollick's line is the right framing for Apollo's agentic bank run note: a lot of systems only work today because friction keeps people from optimizing.

Torsten Slok's version is deposits. Checking pays ~0.1%. Fintechs pay 3-5%. Household inertia is the moat. An agent that sweeps cash for yield removes that moat at machine speed.

The same pattern shows up in software:
1. Manual review that only works because volume is low
2. Nobody will bother security assumptions
3. Pricing that depends on customers not shopping every week

If your product or process needs human laziness to stay stable, treat that as a bug, not a feature. Design for the day the agent removes the friction.
hits.video_tip: Cut the Apollo yield bar chart for 8 seconds, then a whiteboard: Friction -> Inertia -> Cheap deposits. Cross out Inertia. 40 seconds.

hits.name: Ethan Mollick
hits.hook: Mollick used Opus 5.5 to make a Connections-style video of the contingent path into the current AI moment.
hits.draft_en:
Ethan Mollick had Opus 5.5 build a Connections-style video about the random contingencies that produced today's AI acceleration.

The useful move is not AI made a cool explainer. It is using a model to surface the non-obvious dependency chain: which ideas, papers, and accidents had to line up.

I would steal the format for internal work:
- Why did this product decision become inevitable?
- Which three bets had to work for our agent stack to ship?
- What would a junior engineer miss if they only read the launch blog?

Ask for a timeline of contingencies, not a victory lap. The value is in the junctions, not the montage.
hits.video_tip: MEDIA WARNING: 3-minute video; only saw the thumbnail. Screen-record 20 seconds of the opening frame, then cut to your own 3-node contingency map.

hits.name: Ethan Mollick
hits.hook: Mollick: the open vs closed gap widened; Fable/Astra-class models are agentic in a way open models are not yet.
hits.draft_en:
Ethan Mollick's qualitative read matches what I see in day-to-day agent work: the open vs closed gap is wider again, and the split is about agency, not chat quality.

Fable/Astra-class models plan, call tools, and recover from failed steps in a way that changes the product shape. Pre-Fable models and current open weights still need you to hold the loop.

What that means practically:
- Keep your skill API and memory layer model-agnostic
- Measure tasks finished without a human nudge, not just tokens/sec
- When open models cross that line, expect a jump, not a gentle catch-up

Do not rebuild your stack around one closed model. Build so you can swap the day an open model starts finishing the job.
hits.video_tip: Talking-head, 30 seconds: two columns on a notepad, Closed vs Open. Circle unassisted task completion.

reply_now.name: Philipp Schmid
reply_now.reply_draft: Env vars are not a secret boundary inside an agent sandbox. Anything the process can read, a dependency can exfiltrate. Inject secrets on the wire for trusted domains only, and keep raw tokens out of the sandbox filesystem.

reply_now.name: Ethan Mollick
reply_now.reply_draft: Eternal September is a content ops problem as much as a culture one. Keep a one-page what changed this quarter note with durable claims only: permissions, evals, cost. Reuse it every time a new audience rediscovers the same debates.

reply_now.name: Ethan Mollick
reply_now.reply_draft: The Connections format works when it maps contingencies, not vibes. I would run the same prompt on our own stack: which three unrelated bets had to land for the agent workflow to ship. The junctions are the lesson.

reply_now.name: Ethan Mollick
reply_now.reply_draft: BLEU and ROUGE answer string overlap. Agents fail on tool choice, unsafe actions, and unfinished jobs. If the scorecard cannot show task success plus intervention rate, it is measuring the wrong system.

reply_now.name: Ethan Mollick
reply_now.reply_draft: The gap that matters is unassisted loop completion, not chat quality. Keep skills and memory model-agnostic so you can swap the day an open model starts finishing the job without a babysitter.

reply_now.name: Hamel Husain
reply_now.reply_draft: The part to watch is whether query-plus-inference planning holds on messy multi-join workloads, not the launch meme. If throughput stays real, warehouse-touching agents stop being a cost joke.

reply_now.name: Hamel Husain
reply_now.reply_draft: Same rule I use: treat every judge as a classifier. Label a trusted set, report TPR and TNR, and only then scale. Accuracy on imbalanced eval data is how teams fool themselves.

reply_now.name: Jerry Liu
reply_now.reply_draft: Agree. When a happy user can stand up an equivalent stack in two days, sales packaging is part of the product. Compliance paperwork as an upsell is how you donate the account to self-host.
